source: Widely circulated 'Supermarket sales' dataset (attributed on Kaggle to Aung Pyae). Copy used: Plotly public datasets repository.
license: The Plotly datasets repository is MIT-licensed. The original Kaggle upload lists its license as unspecified/other and is broadly used for education. Treat as: freely usable for research with attribution; not a formally licensed corpus.
citation: Aung Pyae. Supermarket sales [Data set]. Kaggle. https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/aungpyaeap/supermarket-sales  (copy obtained via https://github.com/plotly/datasets)
country_context: Myanmar (branches in Yangon, Mandalay, Naypyitaw). South/Southeast Asian emerging-market retail. NOT India.
business_domain: Supermarket retail across 6 product lines; one row per invoice; includes cost of goods and gross income (real margin fields).
data_type_note: The uploader describes it as historical records for a supermarket company over 3 months in 3 branches; several secondary sources treat it as simulated/anonymised. Conservatively marked 'mixed' (semi-synthetic).
known_limitations: Myanmar, not India. Used only for regional emerging-market relevance; the paper must not call it Indian.
Only 89 days and 18 (branch x product-line) series after aggregation - a very small forecasting set; results are illustrative, high-variance.
Provenance is ambiguous (real vs simulated); marked 'mixed'.
No marketing-spend or promotion field; the forecasting adapter holds marketing_spend and promotion_flag at 0.
The analytics file (revenue/cogs/gross_income/margin_pct) is NOT consumed by any current DecisionGPT model; it is provided for descriptive business analytics only.
Only ~89 days total; the chronological test split is tiny (~50 rows), so forecasting metrics are high-variance and illustrative only.
